Title: Natural Energy Resources
Content: Humans use many types of natural resources to provide energy for their `text(daily)` lives. Petroleum, also called crude oil or oil, is a fossil fuel formed `text(millions of years)` ago. It is an important fuel source used around the world. Oil can be refined to produce heating fuel and gasoline. It can also be used to produce electrical energy.
Oil is found in pockets under `text(Earth’s)` surface. The photograph below shows an oil seep. Oil seeps occur when crude oil leaks through natural cracks in the ocean floor.
The model below represents the positions of both the oil pocket and oil seep in relation to the ocean floor. The direction of motion of oil droplets in the ocean is indicated.

Offshore drilling is a way of obtaining underground oil from `text(Earth)` by drilling into the ocean floor where oil pockets have been found. In `2019`, New York State passed a law banning offshore drilling in the ocean floor within `text(three miles)` of the state’s shoreline.

Wind is another natural resource that humans use to provide energy for their `text(daily)` lives. Wind is used to produce electricity with large windmills called wind turbines. A wind farm is a group of wind turbines in the same location. The photograph below shows Maple Ridge Wind Farm, located in Lewis County, New York.
